extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and authors (novelists and short-story writers) looking to develop character voice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating a strong, authentic character voice in fiction by using cultural background, upbringing, location, values, occupation, personality, speech habits (greetings/slang/cursing), and consistent choices to shape what the character notices and how they speak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character voice (definition & importance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters are possibly the most important part of a book; character voice involves all of their background and quirks, all of the personal behaviors and ways they speak that your readers will relate to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If readers connect with your characters they'll follow them through the story. Character voice shapes what a character notices and how they describe things; building a strong character voice increases reader connection and makes characters feel authentic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural background
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider what cultural worldview your character will be coming from: common behaviors, forbidden behaviors, and common images/symbols used to illustrate concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cultural details (customs, symbols, taboos) to shape interactions and descriptions. Things out of keeping with a character’s cultural background will catch their attention and can be a tool for highlighting details. Example: Duyên notices guests failing to remove shoes; she uses cultural symbols (dragons, phoenixes) in imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upbringing (personal history)
rubrics_metrics.description: The way your character has been treated over the course of their life will impact their voice and worldview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at a character’s history to determine how upbringing shapes perception of issues, self, and others. Contrast examples (loving family vs. slave background) produce different voice emphases (attachment to family vs. avoidance). Use upbringing to explain feelings of belonging, worth, and reactions to social settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical location (environmental imagery)
rubrics_metrics.description: A character's physical surroundings influence their imagery and comparisons (e.g., desert imagery vs. ocean imagery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have the character use images and metaphors drawn from their environment (sand, waves, fish, salt, etc.). Establish the source of these comparisons for the reader—if the setting that supplies those metaphors hasn't been hinted at, the metaphors will confuse readers. Examples: fishing-village metaphors used because neighboring towns fish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal values (what the character notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: A character’s values determine what they observe and prioritize in narration and thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide what your character values (community, beauty, leadership, etc.) to focus descriptions and internal attention. Examples: a character who values community notices people; a leader notices things affecting their ability to lead. Use values to decide which details to show and which to ignore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation and hobbies
rubrics_metrics.description: A character's job or hobbies shape their perceptions and the details they notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vocational and pastime influences to color observations (fisherman notices weather; artist notices light and small details). Influence can vary by importance to the character or situation. Example: Duyên is an author/musician, so she thinks in stories and musical metaphors—include short illustrative snippets to show this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personality
rubrics_metrics.description: Personality affects how a character sees and interacts with the world (introversion vs. outspokenness, emotional attunement, selfishness vs. selflessness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect personality in prose: an emotionally attuned character uses emotional descriptions; a matter-of-fact character uses blunt prose. Challenge: still show emotions for characters who don't notice them themselves. Use personality to shape decisions, reactions, and focalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greetings and farewells (speech habits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine common greetings/farewells in the culture and how the character uses or adapts them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether a character uses full/formal phrases, shortened forms, or substitutes (especially if they reject cultural/religious elements). Consider initiation vs. response (who greets first), non-verbal returns (nods), and whether a character sometimes refrains from returning greetings. Example: Virilia greeting variations and how believers/doubters alter them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slang, metaphors, and idioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the slang, common metaphors, similes, nicknames, terms of endearment, and derogatory terms in the setting and whether/how the character uses them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide which slang and idioms the character uses, with whom, and in what situations. Consider nonstandard usages (e.g., derogatory words used affectionately, or condescending uses). Using distinctive slang can develop voice but requires consistency and contextual clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cursing (real vs. invented)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the character would realistically curse and why, and whether to use real-world curses or invented ones in a secondary world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know whether a character refrains from cursing for moral reasons, habit, or creativity. Invented curses often fit better in secondary worlds; real-world curses can feel out-of-place. Different characters’ attitudes toward curses can create interpersonal dynamics or internal conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and complexity of voice
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong character voice is both complex and consistent across background, values, habits, and language choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine cultural background, upbringing, location, values, occupation, personality, and speech habits into a coherent, consistent voice so readers can connect. Expect complexity—many elements contribute to voice—but maintain internal consistency so voice feels authentic rather than muddled.
